newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Jul-Sept temperatures seen average to low.
newsitem.headline: Japan Jul-Sept temperatures seen average to low.

text.p: Temperatures are forecast to be average to lower than average in Japan during the three months from July to September, the Meteorological Agency said on Thursday.
Rainfall during the period is expected to be average to heavy, it said in its three-month weather report.
Temperatures and rainfall are forecast to be about normal for the period in northern Japan and the southwestern islands.
However, eastern and western Japan are likely to see lower than normal temperatures and heavier than usual rainfall during the three months.
The rainy season is expected to last longer than the average year in northern, eastern and western Japan, it said.
In a breakdown of each month, the agency said they expected more cloudy and rainy days than average in July.
Temperatures are expected to be about average in northern Japan and the southwestern islands, while low temperatures are forecast for eastern and western Japan.
Rainfall is expected to be about average in northern Japan and the southwestern islands, and heavier than usual in eastern and western Japan.
In August, temperatures are expected to be about average in the southwestern islands, and low in northern, eastern and western Japan. Rainfall is expected to be about average.
September is expected to see periods when the weather is overcast. Temperatures and rainfall are expected to both be about average.
The agency also referred to the El Nino weather phenomenon, although it stopped short of saying it was forming.
"There is a possibility that we will see (El Nino)," an agency spokesman said.
It said past data showed that summer temperatures tended to be average to low nationwide when the phenomenon occurred.
It also said the rainy season tended to last longer.
The number of typhoons that form appear to be less than average on an annual basis, the agency said.
Meteorologists say there are signs the El Nino weather phenomenon -- which occurs every two to seven years -- is starting to form but its strength will not be known until August.
